text: job-deliverable-v1 task=k7a7f086576 | With PgBouncer transaction pooling, a server connection is returned after each transaction, so a later transaction may land on a different PostgreSQL backend. Prepared statements are backend-session state. If the client uses SQL PREPARE/EXECUTE, or protocol-level named statements without PgBouncer tracking, EXECUTE on a backend that never saw the prepare fails with SQLSTATE 26000, class invalid_sql_statement_name: ‘prepared statement … does not exist.’ Mitigation: use session pooling (or, for extended-protocol statements, enable PgBouncer max_prepared_statements>0). Tradeoff: session pooling loses much of transaction pooling’s connection compression; tracking adds memory and rewrite/cache overhead.  Separately, PostgreSQL plan_cache_mode=auto uses custom plans for the first 5 executions, then builds a generic plan and compares its estimated cost with the average custom-plan cost. Parameter skew can make that generic plan much slower in reality, causing a sudden latency jump around execution 6. Mitigation: force_custom_plan for affected statements. Tradeoff: every execution pays planning CPU/latency and loses generic-plan reuse.
